clue.text: Murder detectives follow one into house

indicators.note: the word into tells us one group of letters is placed inside the house word

parts.note: a house is a home

indicators.note: the detectives come after the one, so follow fixes the order of the inner pair

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK police detective branch

explanation.surface: Police detectives arrive after someone enters a house where a killing took place.
explanation.walkthrough: CID, the UK police detective branch, is a fixture of crosswords; 'follow' puts it after the one before both go 'into' the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name the unlawful killing of a person; one is the legal term for the other.

clue.text: Funny guy Roy and the French get together

parts.note: Roy Hudd was a British comedian
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A comedian and some French people meet up.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy Hudd was a well-known British comic and radio comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: To cluster closely as a group is to come together in a tight knot.

clue.text: Harry and Adrian on the way

parts.note: Adrian Mole is the teenage diarist of Sue Townsend's books
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A man named Harry and his friend Adrian travel along a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a man's name but is the verb meaning to pester; Adrian Mole is the hero of Sue Townsend's comic diaries.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to harass or pester them, which this verb also covers.

clue.text: Interprets studies on the northern French roads

parts.note: to con is to study, so studies gives cons
in northern English dialect the is shortened to t', as in t'mill
rue is French for street, plural rues

explanation.surface: A scholar studies the roads of northern France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the northern' is T' (dialect for 'the' in Yorkshire and Lancashire), not anything about the north of France.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe a remark is to read a particular meaning into it, i.e. explain it.

clue.text: Done like this grid

definitions.meaning: done is British slang for cheated or swindled
the grid has many letters checked both across and down, crossed twice over

explanation.definitionFit: Done means betrayed or cheated; a crossword grid's squares are crossed by two sets of lights.

clue.text: Make light of things?

parts.note: read not as treating something as trivial but literally as making things paler in colour, which is what a whitening agent does

explanation.surface: An invitation to treat matters lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitening chemical literally lightens the colour of fabrics and other things.

clue.text: Shoot a hen

definitions.meaning: in gardening a shoot bent into the soil to root is so called
a hen kept for its eggs is one that lays

explanation.definitionFit: A gardener's rooting stem and an egg-producing hen both carry this name.

clue.text: Flying one through it to turn about

parts.note: a means one
via means through or by way of

indicators.note: to turn tells us the word it is flipped round to read backwards

parts.note: on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: An aircraft flies through something, then turns back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' makes TI from IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviation is the practice of operating aircraft, in other words air travel by plane.

clue.text: Don Smith unfortunately is last

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Poor Don Smith finishes at the back of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges DON SMITH.
explanation.definitionFit: The one farthest behind in a line is at the very rear position.

clue.text: First to question uncle: I deny criminal misbehaviour

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or wrong, so the letters are bent out of order
First to points at the opening letter of the next word only

explanation.surface: An interrogation begins: the uncle denies any wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First to' takes Q from 'question'; 'criminal' scrambles Q with UNCLE, I and DENY. 'criminal' looks like part of the definition but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Delinquency is wrongdoing, especially minor crime by the young, so it is a form of bad conduct.

clue.text: After dark John Harrison is a security guard

parts.note: after dark is night time
John Harrison was the clockmaker who built the marine chronometer, a maker of watches

explanation.surface: A clockmaker on the night shift is protecting a building.
explanation.walkthrough: John Harrison was the 18th-century English clockmaker whose timepieces solved longitude at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A person employed to guard premises overnight is a watchman working the night shift.

clue.text: Bar of thin nickel

indicators.note: of here means the letters come out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A bar made from a thin piece of nickel metal.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'thIN Nickel'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub, where drinks are served at a bar, is an alternative word for a tavern or bar.

clue.text: Pianist's record heard

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for record is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to list things is to record them

explanation.surface: A concert pianist's recording is listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian virtuoso pianist and composer; 'Pianist's' is Pianist plus 's for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hungarian composer was the most famous keyboard virtuoso of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Record the sound of a beat by exponent producing the number

parts.note: a log is a written record

indicators.note: the sound of says the words a beat are replaced by something that is pronounced like them

parts.note: a beat is a rhythm, giving a rhythm

explanation.surface: Logging the sound of a drum beat alongside a mathematical value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rhythm' said aloud gives ARITHM.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a logarithm is the power to which a base must be raised to give a given value.

clue.text: Cut E on a bus when stoned. Me and you get hypodermic

indicators.note: stoned means high on drugs, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: me and you together are us

explanation.surface: Getting high on ecstasy on a bus, the pair inject themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when stoned' scrambles CUT E ON A BUS into SUBCUTANEO; E is slang for the drug ecstasy, adding to the drugs picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypodermic injection goes beneath the skin, which is what the longer medical word means.

clue.text: Like Number 10, Tory spins spin by a Labour leader

indicators.note: spins means turns round, so the Tory word is read backwards

parts.note: con is short for Conservative, a Tory
a turn is a spin

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: Downing Street, where Tory spin doctors work alongside a Labour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number 10' is not Downing Street but 10-down, the NIGHTWATCHMAN, who works at night. 'spins' turns CON into NOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A night guard is active during the hours of darkness, like an owl.

clue.text: Rod? Rod is dancing in town

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

indicators.note: dancing means moving around, so the letters of the second rod shift about

explanation.surface: A man named Rod dances in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Stafford is the county town of Staffordshire in England; 'dancing' rearranges ROD into ORD.
explanation.definitionFit: This English place is the county seat of Staffordshire, a market settlement.

clue.text: To start with Ms Titmuss met with a fool at Number Ten …

parts.note: Abi Titmuss is a British glamour model and TV personality
a nit is a fool
ten written as figures is 1 and 0, which look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: To begin with, a celebrity met an idiot at Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Abi Titmuss was a British tabloid celebrity of the 2000s; 'Number Ten' here is not Downing Street but the digits 1 and 0.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means from the beginning, so it starts at the start.

clue.text: South African cricketer from behind has a firm cheek. Hot stuff!

indicators.note: from behind says the South African cricketer is read starting at its end

parts.note: a bat is a batsman, a cricketer
Co is short for company, a firm
sauce is impudence or cheek

explanation.surface: A cheeky South African batsman joins a company, a hot property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from behind' turns SA BAT into TABAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Louisiana chilli condiment is famously fiery, a hot thing to eat.

clue.text: … but now lives with Mr O'Connor

parts.note: the ellipsis carries on from the previous clue's Ms Titmuss, who supplies ABI
Des O'Connor was a British singer and TV host

explanation.surface: The celebrity has now moved in with a TV host.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 17-down: Ms Titmuss (ABI) is the subject who 'now lives with' Des O'Connor, the British entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide somewhere is to dwell there, an old word for residing.

clue.text: Looks lower first for flowers

indicators.note: first puts the lower in front of the looks

parts.note: a lower is something that lows, as cattle do, so an ox
eyes means looks at, as in to eye

explanation.surface: Someone eyes something lower down before seeing the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' is not 'more low' but 'one that moos'. Ox-eye daisies are the flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye daisy is a common wild bloom with white petals and a yellow centre.

clue.text: Muck is fun to play with as a form of entertainment

indicators.note: to play with suggests toying with the letters, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Messing about in dirt is enjoyable for a child at play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to play with' rearranges MUCK IS FUN.
explanation.definitionFit: This rhythmic, bass-heavy style of popular music is something people listen to for enjoyment.

clue.text: Principal course taken by American officer

definitions.meaning: an American student's main subject of study is their ...

explanation.definitionFit: The word means chief, names a US student's main field of study, and is an army rank above captain.

clue.text: remove something in case …

parts.note: read not as a precaution but literally: taking an item out of its container or packaging

explanation.surface: Taking something away just as a precaution.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the next clue but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To take an item out of its packaging is to free it from its container.

clue.text: … military manoeuvre takes time to select

parts.note: an op is a military operation

explanation.surface: A military operation takes time to choose.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose between alternatives is to make a choice, or pick one.

clue.text: Lady admitted FBI met finally with us lawyer. It's the end of the world!

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the other pieces go inside the lady

parts.note: Judy is a woman's name, as in Punch and Judy
G-men are FBI agents, government men

indicators.note: finally picks only the closing letter of met

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, a US prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A woman lets in FBI agents and an American lawyer, and doom follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady' is the name Judy, which 'admitted' opens around the rest; G-men is old slang for FBI agents and DA a district attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian belief the Last Judgement comes when the world ends.

clue.text: Whatnot is broken by door

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture is damaged by a door.
explanation.walkthrough: A doobry is British slang for a thingummy, something whose name escapes you; 'broken' rearranges BY DOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang placeholder words for an item whose name you cannot recall.

clue.text: Psychotherapy say, in LA's unusual

indicators.note: unusual signals that the preceding letters appear in an unexpected order

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, taken with its s

explanation.surface: Therapy is commonplace in Los Angeles, which is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges SAY IN LAS. 'say' looks like a link to the definition but is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychoanalysis, a talking therapy, is often called simply by this shorter name.
